To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EOC cells can be divided into two subgroups according to their glucose metabolic profile, and that this metabolic phenotype can be used as a predictor of PLT sensitivity and patient outcome.

(1) EOC cells from platinum (PL)-sensitive patients are characterized by glucose deprivation sensitivity (GA) and higher PLT sensitivity, compared to EOC cells from PLT-resistant patients, which are characterized by glucose non-addiction (GNA); (2) the association between PLT resistance and GNA is confirmed by in vivo experiments; (3) in a cohort of EOC patients, GNA is associated with poor clinical outcomes, compared to GA.
glucose metabolism is a metabolic trait of EOC and that it influences response to PLT-based chemotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new molecular trait, the glucose metabolic phenotype, which may be exploited for the identification of patients with EOC who are more likely to benefit from PLT-based treatment.
the identification of a metabolic trait of EOC cells that is predictive of response to PLT-based therapy.
the identification and characterization of GA and GNA EOC cells and the correlation between their metabolic phenotype and response to PLT treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glucose starvation is a metabolic trait of platinum-sensitive EOC cells and that this metabolic trait can be exploited to improve patient selection.
glucose metabolic traits are associated with PLT resistance and may predict response to chemotherapy in patients with EOC.
EOC cells from GA patients are more sensitive to PLT, and that this metabolic trait is associated with better prognosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic profile of cancer cells can be exploited as predictive factor for PLT sensitivity in EOC patients.
glucose starvation resistance can be identified as a metabolic trait of PLT-resistant EOC and that it can be exploited to identify a group of patients with a better clinical outcome.

EOC cells can be categorized into two metabolic groups, glucose-addicted (GA) and glucose non-addicted (GNA) and that the former are more sensitive to PLT and have better outcome, compared to the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glucose starvation resistance is a metabolic trait of PLT-resistant human EOC cells, which is also associated with worse prognosis.

the metabolic phenotype of cancer cells, as defined by their ability to cope with glucose starvation, is a relevant trait that can be used to predict PLT sensitivity and response to chemotherapy in EOC.
glucose starvation is a reliable in vitro tool to predict in vivo sensitivity to PLT in EOC patients.
